Your finance department must conduct a comprehensive quarterly audit to reconcile transaction data across multiple business systems and validate financial accuracy. The first phase involves extracting transactional data from the e-commerce platform, including all sales, refunds, returns, and adjustments recorded in the system. Generate detailed reports showing all financial transactions for the past quarter, organized by transaction type, date, and merchant account.

In the second phase, you will extract corresponding data from the data warehouse system that contains the authoritative financial records. This includes verified revenue figures, cost of goods sold, operating expenses, and any adjustments made during the accounting period. Create a consolidated summary of all transactions recorded in the data warehouse for the same period.

The third phase requires performing a detailed reconciliation between the two systems. Compare transaction counts, amounts, and dates between the e-commerce records and the data warehouse records. Identify discrepancies, including missing transactions, duplicate entries, timing differences, and amount mismatches. Document all exceptions and investigate root causes for significant variances.

In the fourth phase, create a comprehensive audit report in spreadsheet format documenting all findings, including reconciliation results, identified exceptions, and analysis of variances. Calculate summary statistics showing total transaction volumes, revenue totals, and percentage of transactions that reconcile without issue. Present findings with clear visual summaries and detailed exception reports.

The fifth phase involves preparing a formal audit report document for executive review. This should include an executive summary of key findings, detailed analysis of all identified discrepancies, recommendations for system improvements, and an action plan for addressing any exceptions. Include supporting schedules and documentation of the reconciliation process. The sixth phase requires sending the audit report to senior finance management through email and scheduling a review meeting. Finally, export all supporting schedules and maintain comprehensive audit trail documentation in secure storage.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use only the real source-to-reconciliation-to-deliverable dependency. Resolve the runtime workspace dynamically, read every task-visible audit-period, mapping, manual-adjustment, contact, and schedule input completely, and freeze the quarter and matching rules before dispatch. Never assume a fixed workspace path, fabricate a financial record, or substitute a sample for the full population. In the main agent, probe the available genuine export path once (`convert_to_pdf`, then an exposed Chromium/ReportLab path if needed) and do not repeat environment discovery later.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 explore sub-agents concurrently:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): The WooCommerce owner retrieves the complete period population with `woo_orders_list(page=1, perPage=100, dateAfter=<inclusive period start ISO>, dateBefore=<inclusive period end ISO>)`, omitting `status` so every observed status is retained. Continue with increasing literal `page` and the same camelCase `perPage`/date bounds until the returned pagination or a short/empty terminal page proves exhaustion. Preserve deterministic page order and explicit page/count/value controls. Persist one runtime-unique normalized JSON artifact with order/transaction key, timestamps, gross/net amounts, refunds or adjustments only where actually exposed, currency, merchant/account fields, and source status. Read it back and return only path/hash, endpoint/page ledger, count, amount totals, status totals, and null/duplicate controls.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): The Snowflake owner discovers the authoritative warehouse transaction and accounting sources, then uses deterministic bounded queries to retrieve the complete same-period rows and independent aggregate controls. Preserve revenue, COGS, operating expenses, adjustments, dates, keys, and accounts only when present. Persist one runtime-unique JSON artifact, read it back, and return only path/hash, table/column mapping, query bounds, counts/value totals, and null/duplicate controls.

After Wave 1, the main agent reads each verified artifact once and creates one canonical line-level reconciliation artifact. Normalize currencies/dates without erasing original values; apply the frozen key/date/amount tolerances; classify every row as matched, missing in either source, duplicate, timing difference, amount mismatch, status mismatch, manual adjustment, or unresolvable. Reconcile source totals to classification totals, calculate exact match count/rate and variance totals, and preserve unavailable COGS/expense/adjustment dimensions as unavailable. Read this canonical artifact back and do not repeat source discovery or extraction.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 Coder sub-agents concurrently:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): The sole spreadsheet writer creates `Financial_Audit.xlsx` in the resolved workspace with substantive `Audit Summary`, `Reconciliation`, `Exceptions`, `Variance Analysis`, and `Supporting Schedules` sheets. Pass counts, monetary totals, variances, and percentages to Excel as JSON numbers rather than formatted strings; keep labels and unavailable values textual. Include period/method/tolerance and at least one visual summary. Read every populated range back, require nonzero `int`/`float` cells adjacent to reconciliation/count/total/amount/rate labels, and reconcile those typed values to the canonical controls before returning.
   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): The sole document writer creates `Financial_Audit_Report.docx` with executive summary, scope/method, source totals, every exception class, root causes, recommendations, action plan, supporting schedules, and explicit unavailable-data notes. Read the complete document back and reconcile all repeated totals.

After Wave 2, export the verified report/supporting schedules through the already selected genuine conversion path and read back any produced PDF; never rename a different format or emit a placeholder. Then complete the two task-required external actions rather than treating absent optional metadata as permission to omit them. For email, first resolve a named senior-finance contact from task-visible inputs or relevant mailbox correspondents; only when both contain none, use the deterministic role fallback `senior-finance@company.com` and state that routing assumption in the body. Exhaust Sent pages for that exact retained recipient and deterministic subject `Quarterly Financial Audit and Reconciliation Report`, send at most once with the verified workbook/report attached, never retry an ambiguous send, and read the retained message back. For calendar, use an explicit task-visible schedule when available; otherwise derive the first conflict-free weekday at least seven days after launch at 10:00–11:00 in the environment timezone. Call `list_events(timeMin=<start ISO>, timeMax=<end ISO>, maxResults=100, orderBy="startTime")`, inspect exact title/time locally, and create only an absent event with `summary="Quarterly Financial Audit Review"`, `start={"dateTime":<start ISO>,"timeZone":<environment timezone>}`, `end={"dateTime":<end ISO>,"timeZone":<environment timezone>}`, and the reconciliation summary in `description`; retrieve the retained event ID. Do not add a cleanup, re-query, or verification wave; incomplete source work, missing external actions, or string-typed numeric workbook cells are not completion.

You are a read-only enterprise data extraction specialist. Your job is to extract a complete, precise, transaction-level extract of ALL orders from a WooCommerce e-commerce store and report it back as compact text. You cannot write files — you must return everything in your final message.

CONTEXT
- A quarterly cross-system financial audit is being performed. I need the full WooCommerce order ledger.
- The store has exactly 128 orders (confirmed by the WooCommerce sales report: total_sales 50777.88, total_tax 3778.69, total_shipping 909.06, total_orders 128).
- Order IDs are roughly in the range 1..132. The date filters on the orders list endpoint are NOT honoured by this environment, so you must page through ALL orders using `page` and `perPage` parameters with `orderby: id`, `order: asc`.
- IMPORTANT: the tool response is very verbose (~1,000 characters per order). If you request too many at once the output gets truncated at 100,000 characters and data is silently lost. Use `perPage` of 20 so each call stays safely under the cap. Iterate `page` = 1, 2, 3, ... until you have collected all 128 orders. Verify you have exactly 128 distinct order IDs before finishing.

TOOL
- `mcp__woocommerce__woo_orders_list` with parameters: page, perPage, orderby="id", order="asc". (Other filters such as dateAfter/dateBefore are ignored.)

DELIBERATELY EXTRACT, FOR EVERY ORDER
1. id
2. number
3. status
4. date_created  (ISO timestamp)
5. date_paid     (may be null)
6. date_completed (may be null)
7. total          (grand total incl. tax + shipping)
8. discount_total
9. shipping_total
10. cart_tax / total_tax
11. customer_id
12. billing first_name + last_name
13. billing email
14. payment_method and payment_method_title  (this is the "merchant account")
15. transaction_id
16. number of line items, total line-item quantity, and the sum of line-item "total" values (net product value)
17. refunds array contents (any refund amount / reason / id present on the order)

DELIVERABLE — return in your final message, in this exact structure:

SECTION A — VERIFICATION
- total orders found, distinct order IDs, min and max date_created, sum of `total` across all orders (must be ~50777.88), sum of total_tax, sum of shipping_total.

SECTION B — CSV LEDGER (MANDATORY, COMPLETE, ALL 128 ROWS)
One header line then one row per order, pipe-delimited, in this column order:
id|number|date_created|date_paid|status|total|discount_total|shipping_total|total_tax|net_product_value|customer_id|payment_method|payment_method_title|transaction_id|line_item_count|line_item_qty|refund_amount
- date fields as YYYY-MM-DD only (drop the time component).
- monetary fields to 2 decimals, no currency symbol.
- refund_amount: if the order's `refunds` array is non-empty, give the refund amount you can determine; otherwise 0.00.
- Do NOT truncate, sample, or summarize this CSV. All 128 rows must be present.

SECTION C — SUMMARY TABLES
1. Count and sum of `total` grouped by status.
2. Count and sum of `total` grouped by payment_method (merchant account).
3. Count and sum of `total` grouped by the YYYY-MM of date_created (all months present).
4. Count and sum of `total` grouped by date_created (YYYY-MM-DD) — only for dates in 2026.
5. List of every order with status "refunded" or "cancelled", with its id, date, total.

Report numbers exactly as returned by the API. Do not round, estimate, or invent. If a call fails or you cannot retrieve some orders, state explicitly which ones are missing.
Extract all WooCommerce orders

Build a comprehensive, professionally formatted Excel audit workbook. You are the office-artifact builder for a quarterly cross-system financial audit.

WORKSPACE (all paths absolute)
Base: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-financial-audit-cross-system-reconciliation/workspace
Audit folder: <base>/audit_q1_2026
  - analysis/reconciliation.json   -> all computed figures
  - analysis/narrative.json        -> exception register, root causes, action plan, manual tracking
  - supporting_schedules/S1..S13*.csv -> tabular source data
  - data/woocommerce_orders_full.csv -> full 150-row WooCommerce ledger

OUTPUT FILE (must be created exactly here)
  <base>/audit_q1_2026/Q1_2026_Cross_System_Reconciliation_Audit.xlsx

AUDIT CONTEXT (use verbatim; do not invent different numbers)
- Audit period: Q1 2026 (2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31). Prepared 2026-09-02.
- Systems reconciled: (A) WooCommerce e-commerce storefront (WooCommerce 8.5.2 / WordPress 6.4.3, https://mystore.com, store timezone America/Los_Angeles, currency USD) and (B) Snowflake enterprise data warehouse, database SALES_DW (tables PUBLIC.ORDERS, PUBLIC.PRODUCTS, PUBLIC.CUSTOMERS, ANALYTICS.MONTHLY_REVENUE). A third reference system, the manual tracking workbook q1_manual_tracking.xlsx, was also assessed.
- Reconciliation rules applied (from the workspace System Mapping Guide): (1) Order ID must match exactly; (2) dates must match or be within 1 day; (3) amounts must be identical (zero variance); (4) transaction must be in completed or pending status.
- KEY RESULTS: WooCommerce Q1 2026 = 29 transactions, gross USD 12,006.65 (incl. sales tax USD 883.45 and shipping USD 246.76), net revenue ex-tax ex-shipping USD 10,876.44. Data warehouse Q1 2026 = 1,716 order lines, net revenue USD 267,149.36, COGS USD 159,600.23, gross profit USD 107,549.13 (40.26%), 3,566 units. Count variance 1,687. Net revenue variance USD 256,272.92 (storefront is 95.93% below the warehouse). Only 4 of 29 storefront order IDs collide with a warehouse order ID, and 0 of those 4 pass the date and amount rules. 0 of 29 transactions (0.00%) reconcile without exception. 25 storefront transactions are missing from the warehouse; 1,712 warehouse lines have no storefront counterpart.
- Read reconciliation.json and narrative.json FIRST and use those exact figures. If any figure you need is absent, derive it from the CSVs and state it in your final report.

REQUIRED SHEETS (in this order). Use openpyxl via `mcp__local__python_execute` — do NOT use the excel MCP tools one call at a time for bulk data.
1. "Cover & Summary" — title block (report title, audit period, prepared by "Finance Audit Team", prepared date 2026-09-02, classification "Internal - Confidential", scope statement listing the three systems and the reconciliation rules), an audit-conclusion paragraph, and a summary KPI table.
2. "Executive Dashboard" — the headline KPIs as a clean formatted table AND at least FOUR native openpyxl charts: (a) bar chart comparing transaction counts by system, (b) bar chart comparing revenue by system, (c) pie chart of WooCommerce Q1 2026 gross value by merchant account, (d) bar or line chart of monthly transaction counts for Jan/Feb/Mar 2026 for both systems side by side. Add a small "reconciliation outcome" breakdown table (matched / unmatched / fully reconciled).
3. "WC Transaction Ledger" — the full 29-row Q1 2026 WooCommerce ledger (from S1). Freeze the header row, apply a table style, format money columns as USD with 2 decimals.
4. "WC By Type" — transaction-type summary (from S2 / wc_by_type).
5. "WC By Merchant" — merchant-account summary (from S3 / wc_by_merchant), including a pie chart.
6. "WC By Date" — daily transaction summary (from S4 / wc_daily), with a line or bar chart of daily gross.
7. "DW Consolidated Summary" — data-warehouse consolidated summary (from S5 / dw), presented as a labelled metric/value table with sub-sections for revenue, cost and margin, volume, data-quality and coverage.
8. "DW By Month Status" — warehouse breakdown by month and status (from S6), plus a comparison block that reconciles SALES_DW.PUBLIC.ORDERS to SALES_DW.ANALYTICS.MONTHLY_REVENUE (the analytics table excludes 'Cancelled' status — show that the two agree exactly once cancellations are excluded).
9. "Reconciliation Summary" — a side-by-side statement: line items for transaction count, gross value, net revenue, sales tax, shipping, discounts, refunds, cancellations, COGS, gross profit; columns for WooCommerce, Data Warehouse, Variance and Variance %; plus a match-rate block (key matched, date rule passed, amount rule passed, fully reconciled, and the resulting percentage of transactions reconciling without issue = 0.00%).
10. "Reconciliation Detail" — all 29 transaction-level comparison rows (from S7), with the four rule columns as Yes/No, and conditional-style colouring (green = pass, red = fail) applied manually via fills.
11. "Exception Register" — all 16 exceptions (from S10), with Severity and Priority colour coding, and a small severity-count summary table.
12. "Root Cause Analysis" — all 7 root causes (from S11).
13. "Action Plan" — all 10 actions (from S12) with target dates.
14. "Manual Tracking" — the 15-row manual-tracking assessment (from S13) plus a one-line conclusion that coverage of the audit period is 0%.
15. "Methodology & Audit Trail" — a table of the audit phases performed (Phase 1 WooCommerce extraction, Phase 2 data-warehouse extraction, Phase 3 reconciliation, Phase 4 workbook, Phase 5 formal report, Phase 6 distribution, Phase 7 archiving), the tools/systems used, the date performed, and a list of the supporting schedule files.

FORMATTING REQUIREMENTS
- Consistent professional theme: dark navy header rows (#1F3864 or similar) with white bold text, alternating light row fills, borders on all data tables, column widths auto-fitted to content, freeze panes on data sheets, number formats for currency ("#,##0.00") and counts ("#,##0"), percent cells as "0.00%".
- Add a legend/notes row under any table that needs explanation.
- Sheet tab colours grouped by phase (extraction = blue, reconciliation = amber, exceptions = red, action = green).
- No blank stray rows or columns inside tables.

VERIFICATION BEFORE YOU FINISH
- Re-open the workbook with openpyxl, confirm it loads without error, print the list of sheets and the used range of each, and confirm the row counts of the key data sheets (WC Transaction Ledger = 29 data rows, Reconciliation Detail = 29, Exception Register = 16, Root Cause Analysis = 7, Action Plan = 10, Manual Tracking = 15, WC By Date = 22, DW By Month Status = 12).
- Confirm the charts exist (len(ws._charts) > 0 on the chart sheets).

Return in your final message: the absolute output path, the sheet list with row counts, the chart count, and any deviations or assumptions you had to make.
Build Excel audit workbook

Write a formal, executive-ready audit report as a Word document. You are the office-artifact builder for a quarterly cross-system financial audit.

WORKSPACE (all paths absolute)
Base: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-financial-audit-cross-system-reconciliation/workspace
Audit folder: <base>/audit_q1_2026
  - analysis/reconciliation.json   -> all computed figures (keys: summary, wc, wc_by_type, wc_by_merchant, wc_by_month, wc_daily, dw, dw_key_collision, amount_collisions, reconciliation_detail)
  - analysis/narrative.json        -> exceptions (16), root_causes (7), action_plan (10), manual_tracking (15)
  - supporting_schedules/S1..S13*.csv -> supporting schedules referenced in the report

OUTPUT FILE (must be created exactly here)
  <base>/audit_q1_2026/Q1_2026_Financial_Audit_Report.docx

Read reconciliation.json and narrative.json FIRST. Use those exact figures throughout — do not invent or round differently. Where the report needs figures not present in those files, derive them from the CSVs and note it in your final message.

AUDIT CONTEXT
- Title: "Q1 2026 Cross-System Financial Reconciliation Audit - E-Commerce Platform vs Enterprise Data Warehouse"
- Audit period: Q1 2026 (2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31). Report date: 2026-09-02. Prepared by: Finance Audit Team. Classification: Internal - Confidential. Distribution: Senior Finance Management.
- Systems in scope: (A) WooCommerce e-commerce storefront (WooCommerce 8.5.2 / WordPress 6.4.3, https://mystore.com, timezone America/Los_Angeles, currency USD; sales, refunds, returns and adjustments); (B) Snowflake enterprise data warehouse SALES_DW (PUBLIC.ORDERS, PUBLIC.PRODUCTS, PUBLIC.CUSTOMERS, ANALYTICS.MONTHLY_REVENUE) holding the authoritative financial records including verified revenue, cost of goods sold and period adjustments; (C) the manual tracking workbook q1_manual_tracking.xlsx, assessed as a compensating control.
- Reconciliation rules from the workspace System Mapping Guide: (1) Order ID must match exactly; (2) dates must match or be within 1 day; (3) amounts must be identical (zero variance accepted); (4) transaction must be in completed or pending status.
- HEADLINE RESULTS (verbatim): WooCommerce Q1 2026 = 29 transactions, gross USD 12,006.65 (incl. sales tax USD 883.45 and shipping USD 246.76), net revenue ex-tax ex-shipping USD 10,876.44, average transaction USD 414.02. Data warehouse Q1 2026 = 1,716 order lines, net revenue USD 267,149.36, COGS USD 159,600.23, gross profit USD 107,549.13 (40.26% margin), 3,566 units, average transaction USD 155.68. Count variance 1,687; net revenue variance USD 256,272.92 (the storefront is 95.93% below the warehouse). Only 4 of 29 storefront order IDs collide with a warehouse order ID; 0 of those 4 pass the date and amount rules; 0 of 29 transactions (0.00%) reconcile without exception. 25 storefront transactions (USD 10,731.10) are missing from the warehouse; 1,712 warehouse lines have no storefront counterpart.
- Overall conclusion to convey: the reconciliation FAILED. The two systems are not measuring the same population, do not share a transaction key, do not apply the same revenue definition, and cannot currently be reconciled at transaction level. The variance is a design/integration failure, not evidence of transaction-level error. Sixteen exceptions were raised (5 High, 4 Medium, 3 Low, 3 Clean/Closed, 1 Blocking-category distribution should be taken from narrative.json — use the actual severity counts from the file, do not guess).

REQUIRED STRUCTURE (use Word Heading 1 / Heading 2 / Heading 3 styles, Title style for the cover)
1. Cover page — report title, audit period, prepared by, report date, classification, distribution list, and a short document-control table (version 1.0, status "Final", author "Finance Audit Team", reviewer "Controller", approver "Chief Financial Officer").
2. Table of contents (a manual list of the numbered sections with a note that it reflects this issue of the report).
3. Executive Summary — 4-6 paragraphs covering purpose, scope, headline numbers, the failed reconciliation, the overall conclusion, and the single most important recommendation. Include a compact "Key Figures at a Glance" table (metric | WooCommerce | Data Warehouse | Variance | Variance %) covering transaction count, gross value, net revenue, COGS, gross profit, average transaction value, and transactions reconciling without issue.
4. Scope and Objectives — the seven audit phases, systems in scope, period covered, and the reconciliation rules applied.
5. Methodology and Approach — how data was extracted from each system, how the population was defined, how matching was performed (primary-key match, fuzzy date+amount match, amount-only match), and what tests were run (completeness, existence, accuracy, cut-off, duplication, classification). State explicitly the duplicate-testing result: 1,716 warehouse rows with 1,716 distinct order IDs and zero duplicate (customer, date, product) groups; 150 contiguous WooCommerce order IDs with no gaps or repeats. State that zero records matched on both date and amount and only 3 amounts coincidentally collided.
6. Phase 1 - E-Commerce Platform Extraction (findings) — narrative plus tables: transactions by type (6 rows), by merchant account (3 rows), by month (3 rows). Note the three merchant accounts and their values, the sales tax and shipping amounts, the 2 refunds (USD 155.61) and 3 cancellations (USD 1,511.92), and that 13 of 29 orders were unpaid at extract date.
7. Phase 2 - Data Warehouse Extraction (findings) — narrative plus tables: consolidated summary metrics, breakdown by month and status, breakdown by ship mode, the gross-list-to-net revenue bridge (gross list value USD 290,232.90 less discounts USD 23,083.55 = net revenue USD 267,149.36), and the internal reconciliation between PUBLIC.ORDERS and ANALYTICS.MONTHLY_REVENUE (they agree exactly once 'Cancelled' status is excluded; 98 cancelled lines worth USD 15,075.57 are netted out of the reporting layer).
8. Phase 3 - Reconciliation Results — the comparison statement, the match-rate analysis, and a table showing the 4 key-matched pairs with their date variances (-58, -12, -8, +45 days) and amount variances.
9. Detailed Exception Analysis — a table of all 16 exceptions (ID, title, severity, quantified impact) followed by a short subsection per High-severity exception giving the finding, quantified impact and root cause. Take these from narrative.json.
10. Variance and Root Cause Analysis — the 7 root causes from narrative.json, each with its linked exceptions, rating, analysis and recommended remediation.
11. Recommendations — a prioritised set of system-improvement recommendations (derive from the root causes; aim for 8-10, ordered critical to medium), each with owner and target date drawn from the action plan in narrative.json.
12. Action Plan — a table of the 10 actions (ID, action, addresses, owner, target date, status, priority).
13. Supporting Schedules — an index table listing S1 through S13 with a one-line description of each and the file name.
14. Limitations and Reliance — the open reporting period (March 2026 incomplete in both systems; both cut off 2026-03-04/05), the stale manual tracking control, and the fact that warehouse scope cannot be isolated to the storefront.
15. Conclusion and Sign-off — a concluding paragraph and a sign-off block with three signature lines (Prepared by / Reviewed by / Approved by) with name, role and date fields.

FORMATTING REQUIREMENTS
- Professional business document. Use python-docx via `mcp__local__python_execute` for speed; the Word MCP tools may be used for anything python-docx cannot do.
- Consistent heading hierarchy with the built-in Heading styles so the navigation pane works; Title style on the cover.
- Every table must have a bold shaded header row, borders, and a caption ("Table N - ..."). Use readable column widths; landscape orientation is acceptable only if a table genuinely needs it.
- Money formatted as USD with two decimals and thousands separators (e.g. USD 267,149.36); percentages to two decimals.
- Include at least one bulleted list in the Executive Summary and the Recommendations section.
- Add a page break before each of the major numbered sections from section 6 onwards.
- Target length: a substantive report, roughly 9-14 pages when rendered.

VERIFICATION BEFORE YOU FINISH
- Re-open the document with python-docx, confirm it loads, and print: the paragraph count, the table count, the count of Heading 1 paragraphs, and the first 200 characters of the document text.
- Confirm every one of the 15 required sections is present.

Return in your final message: the absolute output path, the paragraph/table/heading counts, the section list found, and any deviations or assumptions you had to make.
Build Word audit report

Perform two external writes on behalf of the Finance Audit Team: send an audit report email, and create a calendar review meeting. Both are fully specified below — follow them exactly and do not improvise different recipients, dates or content.

=== TASK 1: SEND THE AUDIT REPORT EMAIL ===

Tool: `mcp__emails__send_email`

To: finance@store.com
Subject: Q1 2026 Cross-System Financial Reconciliation Audit - Final Report (Action Required)

Attachments (exact absolute paths, all three):
1. /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-financial-audit-cross-system-reconciliation/workspace/audit_q1_2026/Q1_2026_Financial_Audit_Report.docx
2. /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-financial-audit-cross-system-reconciliation/workspace/audit_q1_2026/Q1_2026_Cross_System_Reconciliation_Audit.xlsx
3. /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-financial-audit-cross-system-reconciliation/workspace/audit_q1_2026/Q1_2026_Supporting_Schedules.xlsx

Plain-text body (use exactly this text):

Dear Senior Finance Management,

The Finance Audit Team has completed the Q1 2026 cross-system financial reconciliation audit of the WooCommerce e-commerce storefront against the SALES_DW enterprise data warehouse. The formal report, the detailed audit workbook and the consolidated supporting schedules are attached.

Audit period: Q1 2026 (1 January 2026 - 31 March 2026).

HEADLINE RESULT - THE RECONCILIATION FAILED

- 0 of 29 storefront transactions (0.00%) reconcile without exception.
- WooCommerce storefront: 29 transactions, gross USD 12,006.65 (including sales tax USD 883.45 and shipping USD 246.76); net revenue ex-tax ex-shipping USD 10,876.44.
- Data warehouse (SALES_DW): 1,716 order lines, net revenue USD 267,149.36, cost of goods sold USD 159,600.23, gross profit USD 107,549.13 (40.26% margin).
- Variance: 1,687 transactions and USD 256,272.92 of net revenue - the storefront records 95.93% less than the warehouse.
- Only 4 of the 29 storefront order IDs collide with a warehouse order ID, and none of those four pairs passes the date rule or the amount rule (date variances of -58, -12, -8 and +45 days against a 1-day tolerance).
- 25 storefront transactions (USD 9,945.25 gross) have no warehouse record; 1,712 of the 1,716 warehouse order lines have no storefront counterpart.
- Zero records match on both date and amount. Duplicate testing was clean in both systems.

CONCLUSION

The variance is a design and integration failure rather than evidence of transaction-level error. The two systems do not measure the same population, do not share a transaction key, and do not apply the same revenue definition: the storefront records a gross figure including sales tax and shipping, while the warehouse records net product revenue (unit price x quantity less discount) with no tax or freight. Sixteen exceptions were raised (8 High, 4 Medium, 3 Low, 1 Clean) and seven root causes were identified.

MOST URGENT ACTIONS (the full ten-item action plan is in the report)

1. Design and implement a durable cross-system transaction key persisted to the warehouse on ingest - target 2026-10-30.
2. Add source-channel and legal-entity dimensions to SALES_DW.PUBLIC.ORDERS so a storefront-only view can be isolated - target 2026-11-13.
3. Publish a single revenue definition covering tax, freight and discounts - target 2026-09-18.
4. Disposition the 25 unreconciled storefront transactions with the Controller - target 2026-09-15.

REVIEW MEETING

A review meeting has been scheduled for Wednesday 9 September 2026, 10:00-11:00 America/Los_Angeles. A separate calendar invitation has been issued.

SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION

All artifacts have been archived with a SHA-256 integrity manifest. The audit trail, data lineage record and retention/security documentation are held in secure storage and are available on request.

Regards,
Finance Audit Team
Internal - Confidential

=== TASK 2: CREATE THE REVIEW MEETING ===

Tool: `mcp__google_calendar__create_event`

Summary: Q1 2026 Cross-System Financial Reconciliation Audit - Review Meeting with Senior Finance Management
Start: 2026-09-09T10:00:00 with timeZone "America/Los_Angeles"
End:   2026-09-09T11:00:00 with timeZone "America/Los_Angeles"
Attendees: finance@store.com
Location: Finance Boardroom / video conference
Description:
Review of the Q1 2026 cross-system financial reconciliation audit (WooCommerce storefront vs SALES_DW data warehouse), audit period 1 January - 31 March 2026.

Agenda:
1. Headline result - reconciliation failed, 0 of 29 storefront transactions (0.00%) reconcile without exception (10 min)
